name: Mudlick Mountain
summary: Steel fire tower on Mudlick Mountain in Sam A. Baker State Park, Wayne County, MO; standing by 1935, reported 85 ft; last dated mention 1972-73; current condition not confirmed.
other_names: Sam A. Baker State Park Fire Tower
design: Steel four-legged tower with an enclosed observing room at the top (1963 NGS description)
status_note: No source read confirms the tower's condition after a 1972-73 road-work mention; present condition not confirmed
agency: Missouri Conservation Commission (towersite owner per 1947-48 state manual); located in Sam A. Baker State Park

access.note: Inside Sam A. Baker State Park. MDC lists hiking loops that reach the natural area. No source read says the tower itself is open to climbing.

visit.trail_note: MDC: the 1.5 mile Shut-Ins Trail loop and the 12 mile Mudlick Mountain hiking loop provide access to the natural area.

events.note: Already standing by July 4, 1935, when a newspaper describes it as the great steel fire tower on one of the park's highest points
1947-48 state manual lists the towersite as owned by the Missouri Conservation Commission
Fire burned eight acres of a Wayne County farm and took two hours to bring under control; reported January 10, 1958 (fire date not given)
A towerman at Mudlick discovered a fire (reported January 1958); no name given
National Geodetic Survey station description: about 100 ft tall, four-legged steel structure
FY1972-73 state report: road reshaped at the tower; last dated mention found

conflicts.note: Research (2026-10-09) gives unknown where the source records give standing. The page shows the researched status; please tell us if it is wrong.
